avoid_supplements.name: Echinacea
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Immunostimulant may antagonize rituximab's immunosuppressive effects and reduce therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid during rituximab treatment and for at least 6 months after completion

avoid_supplements.name: Astragalus
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Immune-enhancing supplement may counteract B-cell depletion and reduce drug effectiveness

avoid_supplements.name: Live Attenuated Vaccines
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Rituximab causes B-cell depletion and immunosuppression; live vaccines pose infection risk
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated during and for at least 6 months after rituximab; use only inactivated vaccines

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild immune modulation may theoretically interact with rituximab's mechanism
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution and monitor for changes in disease control

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: May support immune recovery but unlikely to significantly impact rituximab efficacy
caution_supplements.action: May be considered for GI support; select well-studied strains

caution_foods.name: High-dose vitamin D supplementation
caution_foods.mechanism: Vitamin D modulates immune function; excessive intake may theoretically affect immunosuppressive balance
caution_foods.action: Monitor vitamin D levels; maintain physiologic supplementation only

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: Not a CYP substrate, but may have mild immune-modulatory effects
caution_foods.action: No strict avoidance required but limit excessive consumption

monitoring_notes: Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody not metabolized by CYP450 enzymes, making traditional drug-supplement interactions unlikely. Primary concern is immune modulation: avoid immunostimulants that may reduce efficacy and strictly contraindicate live vaccines. Monitor for infection risk given B-cell depletion and maintain appropriate prophylaxis.
